title: Christmas in Philadelphia 2026: markets, skating and city lights
description: Plan Christmas in Philadelphia 2026 with Christmas Village dates and closures, Dilworth Park skating and Franklin Square lights on a practical route.
relatedQueries: Dilworth Park Franklin Square Christmas route
intro: For a Philadelphia Christmas break in 2026, choose three places: Christmas Village at LOVE Park, Dilworth Park beside City Hall and Franklin Square. The first offers a German-inspired market, the second combines local shopping with skating, and the third provides the Electrical Spectacle light show.

The calendar is the crucial detail: Christmas Village closes on 25 December, and Franklin Square also publishes holiday closures. One broad November-to-January range is not enough. This guide compares official information checked on 7 November 2026 and proposes a route with time for each experience. Photographs are archival; the Franklin Square fountain is shown without its 2026 lighting installation.

quickFacts.label: Dilworth Park
quickFacts.value: Winter season from 13 November; skating by session

sections.heading: 1. Christmas Village at LOVE Park: note the pause in its calendar
paragraphs: Christmas Village occupies LOVE Park and areas around City Hall. The organiser describes an outdoor market inspired by German traditions, with gifts, decorations, crafts and refreshments. Its listed street address is 1500 Arch Street, a useful reference for the central location rather than every holiday activity in Philadelphia.

The announced period is 21 November to 27 December 2026. It closes on 23–25 November and 25 December. Ordinary hours are noon–20:00 Sunday to Thursday and noon–21:00 Friday and Saturday. Thanksgiving Day, 26 November, has 09:00–17:00 hours; Christmas Eve, 24 December, has noon–17:00 hours.

Entry to the event area is advertised as free, with food, drinks, shopping and rides paid separately. The organiser allows changes or closures in severe weather, so check daily notices before leaving. The photograph shows an earlier edition and does not establish the actual stalls or installations for 2026.

sections.heading: 2. Dilworth Park: separate the walk, local market and ice session
paragraphs: Dilworth Park lies on City Hall’s west side and brings together several experiences. Center City District’s winter programme begins on 13 November 2026 with Wintergarden, the Rothman Orthopaedics Ice Rink and Made in Philadelphia Holiday Market. The latter is announced through 1 January 2027 and is not another name for Christmas Village.

If you want to skate, give it its own session. The operator describes ninety-minute slots and recommends advance purchases; skate hire and lockers have conditions to review before paying. A late arrival does not extend your session. Walking through the park or looking at lights does not provide access to the ice.

The official pages checked disagree on the rink’s final date: the rink listing shows January, while the main winter page shows February. That does not affect the announced start or this guide’s Christmas period, but a final post-Christmas date is not treated as confirmed. For January or February travel, inspect the actual booking calendar before planning around it.

sections.heading: 3. Franklin Square: free lights, with other activities separate
paragraphs: Holidays in Franklin Square is announced for 19 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. Historic Philadelphia describes its main Electrical Spectacle as free. The fountain and surroundings provide the setting for synchronised lights, while miniature golf, the carousel and other activities have their own conditions.

The general published evening period is 17:00–21:00, with light shows every thirty minutes from 17:00 until closing. Exceptions matter: the site closes on 26 November, 25 December and 1 January, and closes early at 20:00 on 24 and 31 December. Check the specific programme for opening night or another special activity.

The documentary photograph shows the fountain in 2013 without holiday lighting, identifying the place without simulating a current-edition image. Locate Franklin Square at 200 North 6th Street and allow a separate journey from City Hall. Avoid making that section a hurried walk after the group has already spent a long time outdoors.

sections.heading: Choose a date that supports the experiences you want
paragraphs: The 21–22 November weekend falls within Christmas Village’s initial period, followed by a published pause on 23–25 November. On Thanksgiving, 26 November, the market opens with special hours but Franklin Square closes. These are different conditions within the same city break: check venues individually instead of assuming a holiday activates every programme.

Christmas Day is unsuitable for completing all three experiences: Christmas Village and Franklin Square publish closures. Dilworth’s skating page lists special hours that day, subject to bookings and operator notices. This does not promise that every stall, café or service in the park follows the rink’s opening.

sections.heading: A practical route with one or two outings
paragraphs: Group LOVE Park and Dilworth Park because of their proximity around City Hall. Set your skating time first if that is the priority, then use the surrounding time for markets. Eating or shopping in every space is optional: you can use one for gifts and the other for a stroll or particular activity.

Give Franklin Square an afternoon or evening block with its calendar already checked. With children or limited enthusiasm for walking, two outings avoid combining skating, a rushed meal and a race for the final light show. This is an indicative route rather than a promise of identical transfer times for every visitor.

sections.heading: Transport, access and a realistic budget
paragraphs: Christmas Village’s organiser identifies Suburban Station and the 15th Street/City Hall area as public-transport approaches. Plan your journey from accommodation with SEPTA and check service for your date; frequencies and last trains are not published here without verification. Returning from Franklin Square involves checking another departure point.

Separate meals, shopping and ticketed activities from the walks and free light show. The market organiser describes access measures, but these do not establish a continuously accessible route between all three venues. Check entrances, surfaces and skating arrangements according to your needs, along with weather notices close to the visit.

Keep the evening flexible rather than buying overlapping activities to fill every minute. A delayed arrival can be handled by choosing the market or booked session that matters most, then moving the remaining outing to another day when its programme operates.

itinerary: First block: browse Christmas Village on an operating date, allowing time to compare prices and choose stalls. Resolve the 23–25 November pause and Christmas Day closure before booking accommodation around the market.

Second block: continue to Dilworth Park for the local market, Wintergarden or a reserved skating session. Leave time to hire equipment and prepare; late arrival does not extend the ninety-minute slot.

Lights block: dedicate an outing to Franklin Square and check special hours for Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve. Dividing the selection over two afternoons keeps all three places without a rushed transfer.

faq.question: Does Christmas Village open on 25 December 2026?
faq.answer: No. The organiser publishes a Christmas Day closure as well as the 23–25 November pause. The overall date range does not mean uninterrupted daily opening.

faq.question: Is Made in Philadelphia Holiday Market the same as Christmas Village?
faq.answer: No. The former belongs to Dilworth Park’s programme. Christmas Village has its own organiser and a central location in LOVE Park and around City Hall.

faq.question: Is the Franklin Square light show free?
faq.answer: Electrical Spectacle is advertised as free. Other activities, including miniature golf and the carousel, have their own conditions and are not included by that free admission.

faq.question: How long does Dilworth skating continue after Christmas?
faq.answer: The official pages checked show conflicting final dates. For January or February, verify the actual booking calendar with the operator; this guide does not present one final date as confirmed.

conclusion: The break works best as three separate choices: a market, skating and a light show. Check closed dates to select the day, reserve only the activity you want and let the lights accompany a route that fits your group.
